name: Antifeminism
summary: Antifeminism is political opposition to feminism and to the gains of women's and feminist movements. Its adherents treat gender roles as natural or divinely ordained, hold that women are not subordinated or that feminism has already won and now overreaches, and defend the traditional family and gender division of labour against equality measures, abortion rights and, increasingly, queer politics and sex education. It runs from the Stop ERA campaign through post-feminist pundits and the men's rights movement to far-right and religious anti-gender mobilisations.
scope: Antifeminism as the scholarship defines it: a political position and discourse, consciously developed by specific actors, against feminist and women's movements, their political goals and the improvements in women's status they won (Goetz and Mayer 2024, s2), with queer politics and gender diversity added as targets today. Strands the sources name: the New Right, religious-conservative organized antifeminism of Phyllis Schlafly's Stop ERA campaign and Eagle Forum (s3); the American post-feminist antifeminism of pundits such as Kathleen Parker, Kate O'Beirne and Christina Hoff Sommers, which holds that feminism has won and now harms men (Anderson 2014, s1); the men's rights movement and its manosphere successors, as far as the sources present them as antifeminist; and the far-right and religious anti-gender mobilisations the 2024 volume studies across five continents (s2). It includes what these sources present as antifeminism's own claims about gender, the family, sexuality and women's rights. It excludes misogyny as individual attitude and sexism as structural discrimination, which s2 distinguishes from antifeminism, and the positions of the broader movements it joins (the far right, religious conservatism, the New Right's economics) beyond what the sources present as antifeminism's own. Writers who call themselves feminists, though others label them antifeminist, count only as s1 presents them. Esther Vilar's The Manipulated Man (1971), downloaded under this name, never names antifeminism in its text and no defining source names it, so it is not tied to the subject and is not cited.
